chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, does temporary marriage (mut'ah) end when its condition expires, then another man marries her when she becomes free from him, then the first man marries her again when she becomes free from him, three times, and she has had three husbands? Is it permissible for the first one to marry her?' He said, 'Yes, as many as he wishes. This is not like the free woman; this is a hired woman, and she is in the status of slave women.'
And whenever a man maries a woman for temporary marriage and she stipulates upon him that he should not have intercourse with her in her vagina, then he is entitled only to what she stipulated.

key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: She became free from him (contract expired)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for remarrying a temporary wife in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Reported by Zurarah from Imam al-Baqir, this hadith clarifies that temporary marriage (mut'ah) allows for unlimited remarriage between the same couple, distinguishing it from the restrictions on permanent marriage with free women by likening its contractual nature to that of slave women. It further establishes the principle of 'what is stipulated is what is taken,' where specific conditions regarding sexual intercourse limit the husband's rights to those exact terms. This ruling underscores the flexibility of mut'ah as a distinct legal category in Shia fiqh, emphasizing the primacy of agreed-upon conditions within the contract.
